about: What changed on the site, newest first. Shown under the version number (top left). Add an entry for every change people can see and every fix, in the same commit, with the date it went live. kind: new | improved | fixed. Keep it short: one line per change, a few words each, and only the points a visitor would notice; a release of fixes is usually one line. Versions: third number for fixes (1.5.1), second for new features (1.6), first for a redesign.

changes.text: Text in the Reader (T): RF1b beside the pages. Point at a word to read it; click it for its crop and places.
Find, under the text's title: the book searched as you type, in Eva or with the glyph keys.
Text tab: search the book by word or pattern; narrow by section, scribe, language, quire or kind; export.
The text shows as glyphs or in Eva, from a dropdown. FSG and Currier are no longer offered.
The text's ? says how to use it and where it comes from; the keyboard list keeps only the keys that matter.
“How the transcribers read it” and notes on words are gone from the word panel.
Text tab, Pages: a chip beside Reading and Spaces; the set chosen can be edited or deleted from its menu.
New page set: one dialog. Pages and ranges read back as you type; add a range, section, quire or scribe.
The Text button in the Reader's bar has an icon, like Bookmark and Grid beside it.
Text tab: More options ran off narrow windows; popovers now stay inside and close on a click elsewhere or Esc.
Text tab: a page clicked in the strip said “No results” when its results were past the first 150 listed.
Text tab, any transcriber: a word written twice in one line was counted and marked once.
Text tab: an empty strip and filters were drawn when nothing matched; #text alone wrote a broken address.
Text tab: section names under the strip overlapped on a phone; pointing at it mid-search threw an error.
Round diagrams: a word's band reaches the tops and tails of its glyphs (2,180 words on 25 pages).
Rearrange: a pile shows every sheet it holds, even while you move one.
Rearrange lays the book out on the table, a pile for each quire, to move sheets around.
Updates to the foldouts and notes as per review by Lisa Fagin Davis.
The 3D book is smoother, with the paper curling round every fold.
f89v2 no longer shows the book's page edges and a strip of the page beneath it.
Every page you go to turns a leaf, including from Go to, the strip and an unfolded foldout, and the book stays in the same place and size as you turn.
A folded foldout is one leaf like any other: you see its spine panel, and the rest of it appears when you unfold it.
Opened-out foldouts no longer show the edges of the book's pages in the middle of the sheet.
Pages are sharp when you zoom in: they now load at full size from Yale's photographs.
What's new: click the version number at the top left to see what changed, and when.
Unfolding and folding: the panels open one after another, like a map, and the book eases to its new size instead of jumping.
More room for the pages: zoom, the opening's tags and its note share one slim row under the pages, and the bar above stays on one line in narrower windows.
Zoom could not go below 100%. It now goes out to 30%, and stays zoomed out as you turn the pages. (Reported by a reader.)
Notes under the pages were cut off with no way to read the rest. Long notes now have a "more" link that shows the whole note. (Reported by a reader.)
The zoom buttons and their hint covered the bottom of the pages and the page labels.
The pages changed size from one opening to the next, when the bar above them wrapped or a note was longer.
f70r2 was cut off at the right, through the middle of its paragraph. It now shows the whole panel.

f70v2 (Pisces) was far wider than the other pages: its photograph shows the panel opened flat across an extra crease. The crease is now a fold, so folded, f70v2 is a page of normal width, and the flap opens with Unfold.
Links and Go to for 70v2 and 101v opened the following opening. They now open the one where the page shows.

First release: the book in 3D, the Reader with its foldouts, the Info pages on Lisa Fagin Davis's research, bookmarks, a crop tool for re-cutting pages from Yale's photographs, and your own orders of the sheets.
